blocks.heading: Key ideas from this article

items.text: Yes, law is a good career field in India, but treat it as six different branches with very different pay and daily work, not one job.

blocks.heading: Answer to "Is Law a Good Career"

items.text: Law remains a genuinely viable, in-demand field in India, and it is far bigger than the courtroom image most families carry into the decision.
But "good career" does not mean "any LLB, any college, guaranteed courtroom glamour or corporate riches."

It means: real demand exists in specific, well-defined branches, real pay exists for graduates who build deliberately toward those branches, and a genuinely uneven, sometimes brutal, first few years exist too, especially for the litigation path most families default to imagining when they hear "law."

blocks.heading: Law Degree Actually Leads: the Branch Map

items.text: Before comparing pay, it helps to see the actual shape of the field, because "lawyer" as a single job title genuinely undersells how many different careers a law degree opens.

The order below is deliberate, not alphabetical or prestige-based: litigation and corporate/in-house lead because they carry this field's strongest real growth and growth headroom, litigation through a genuine scalable-ownership path once you build your own practice or chamber, corporate and in-house work through the fastest-growing early-career pay ceiling of any branch.
Arguing in court, drafting pleadings, and building a practice under a senior advocate.

blocks.heading: Use the Four Questions Before You Commit

items.text: A generic salary number pulled from a Tier-1 firm's recruiting page, or a relative's opinion that "law is a respectable, safe profession," will not tell you whether this field actually fits your money, your patience, and your target branch.
Law rewards people who can read dense, precise language for hours without losing focus, and who can hold a client's or a judge's attention while explaining something complicated in plain terms.
Check the real fee-to-outcome math for your actual college, not a topper's placement photo from a different institute.

blocks.heading: Spend Money and Time on This

items.text: The four questions tells you whether law fits on paper.
Do not lock in a law college seat before passing all three proofs.
Write one real research memo or case note on an actual legal issue, not a generic "why I want to study law" essay.

blocks.heading: How to Actually Raise Your Income Ceiling

items.text: This field's income ceiling is not fixed by which college you attended; it is set by how deliberately you move from a generic legal credential toward a specific, scarce combination of skills.

The clearest ceiling-raising moves here are: building a genuine sector specialisation, data protection, fintech regulation, IP and patent work, competition law, once basic legal training and one or two strong internships exist; moving from a generalist litigation practice toward a specific court or subject-matter reputation; moving from a corporate firm associate role toward in-house leadership or independent advisory work once a real client network forms; and, for graduates who combine law with another degree, engineering plus IP, commerce plus tax, building a niche few pure-law graduates can match.
None of these are guaranteed outcomes, and none happen from the degree alone.

blocks.heading: Mistakes That Waste the Degree

items.text: Graduates who spend five years without testing litigation, corporate, or policy work through internships often leave college with a strong CV and no real sense of which lane actually fits them.

Since the Supreme Court restored the mandatory three-year practice requirement in May 2025, a fresh graduate can no longer sit most state judicial service exams straight out of college in the way earlier batches could.
In most states, document review and contract-lifecycle work at an LPO does not count as court practice for the new three-year rule.

blocks.heading: 3-Year LLB Vs 5-Year BA-LLB Via CLAT
rows: 5-year integrated BA-LLB or BBA-LLB or BSc-LLB
5 years, entered straight after Class 12 CLAT (for the 26 participating National Law Universities) or individual entrance tests/CUET for other 5-year law schools

CLAT 2026 offered roughly 4,092 undergraduate seats across the 26 NLUs, against tens of thousands of aspirants nationwide. It is a genuine national-level filter, and it front-loads legal training with two to three years of a humanities/social-science degree, which is why NLU graduates are the group most actively recruited by top firms, the judiciary track, and large in-house teams.
3-year LLB (after any bachelor's degree)
3 years, open to graduates of any stream, including engineering, commerce, or science CLAT-PG style or individual university entrance exams, plus CUET-LLB for several universities

The deliberate strategic route for someone who already has a first degree and wants to combine it with law, an engineer heading into patent and IP work, a commerce graduate heading into tax or securities law, a science graduate into pharma-regulatory work. It costs three fewer years than starting at 18, but you compete for the same jobs as 5-year graduates without the NLU brand most recruiters filter on first.

blocks.heading: Real Pay, Branch By Branch
rows: Litigation / chamber junior (fresh graduate)
Median roughly Rs 14,000 a month; most fresh graduates land between Rs 5,000-30,000 a month depending on the senior advocate

Some chambers pay nothing in the first year at all, treating the arrangement as training. A handful of established seniors pay Rs 80,000-90,000 a month, but that is the exception, not the median, and it usually goes to a graduate who already interned there repeatedly.
Tier-1 corporate law firm associate (fresher/A0)
Roughly Rs 15-22.5 LPA at firms like Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas, AZB & Partners, Khaitan & Co, Trilegal, Shardul Amarchand Mangaldas, and JSA

This is the number families quote when they say "law pays well," and it is real, but it is not the modal outcome. These seats go overwhelmingly to graduates of the top-ranked NLUs plus a handful of other law schools who clear firm interviews, a small slice of each year's total LLB output.
Mid-size and boutique law firms
Meaningfully below Tier-1 rates, but generally above litigation's early years

Published, verifiable salary data at this tier is thin and firm-specific; treat any number you see here as directional and confirm it against current job postings for the specific firm and city before making a decision.
In-house counsel / corporate legal team
Roughly Rs 18-80+ LPA across the full seniority range; entry-to-mid roles (2-4 years) commonly around Rs 50,000+ a month

The widest range in the field because it spans a fresh graduate's first legal-team role all the way to a general counsel position. Work-life balance is typically stronger than a Tier-1 firm, closer to 9-10 hour days rather than the notoriously long hours associates put in during live deals.
LPO / document review / contract lifecycle
Rs 25,000-45,000 a month at larger LPOs to start, rising toward Rs 70,000 a month within roughly two years; senior legal analyst roles Rs 8-18 LPA

India handles a large share of the world's outsourced legal document work. It is the fastest, most accessible entry point after an LLB, and also the branch where AI-assisted document review is already standard at most mid-to-large operations.
Judiciary (Civil Judge, Junior Division)
Basic pay around Rs 77,840 a month under the Second National Judicial Pay Commission; in-hand typically Rs 90,000-95,000 a month, gross Rs 1-1.45 lakh a month with allowances

One of the strongest guaranteed entry salaries anywhere in the legal field, with a defined pension and promotion ladder. The catch: the Supreme Court restored a mandatory minimum of three years of legal practice as an enrolled advocate before you can even sit this exam in most states, a rule change from 20 May 2025 that closed off the old direct-from-college route.

blocks.heading: NLU Vs Private Law College
rows: Entrance filter
CLAT: a genuine national-level filter with a defined seat count (roughly 4,092 UG seats across 26 NLUs) and heavy competition for the top-ranked ones.

Varies wildly. Some private law schools run a real entrance test; many admit on marks or CUET score alone, so the peer group and rigor differ enormously between institutes with near-identical brochures.
Total cost
Roughly Rs 1.7-4.5 lakh tuition for the full course at most NLUs, modest relative to most professional degrees.
Roughly Rs 2 lakh to over Rs 15 lakh for the same five years, with no reliable link between the fee and placement quality.
Recruiter access
Top-ranked NLUs get direct, on-campus access to Tier-1 firms, the judiciary coaching ecosystem, and large in-house teams; lower-ranked NLUs get meaningfully less of this.
A small number of well-established private law schools run genuinely strong placement cells; most do not, and off-campus effort matters far more for their graduates.
What actually decides your first job
Brand opens the door for Tier-1 firm interviews and judiciary coaching networks, but internship quality, writing samples, and moot court record still do the real filtering once you are in the room.
The degree alone rarely opens a door by itself. Internship record, a genuine writing sample, and direct outreach matter even more here than at a top NLU.

blocks.heading: Who Should Think Twice Before Committing
rows: Choosing law mainly because it "sounds prestigious and stable"

Real income in this field comes from a chosen branch and demonstrated skill, not the label alone. Litigation's early years are genuinely uneven, and even corporate and judiciary tracks now come with new gates, recruiting selectivity and the 2025 practice-first rule, that were not there for earlier graduates.
Assuming any LLB guarantees a corporate firm or judiciary outcome

Tier-1 firm seats and judiciary selection both draw from a genuinely small, competitive slice of each year's graduates. A degree from a college with weak recruiting access needs a specific off-campus plan, not a hope that the qualification alone will do the work.
Picking a high-fee private law college without checking real placement or internship outcomes

Fee and placement quality do not reliably track each other in the private law-college market. A glossy campus and a high fee do not guarantee real internship access, moot court exposure, or corporate recruiting visits.

blocks.heading: Skills That Actually Move the Pay Needle
rows: Legal research using both traditional databases and AI-assisted research tools

Speed matters, but the paid skill in 2026 has shifted toward verifying what an AI tool hands back. The Supreme Court set aside a tribunal ruling in July 2026 built on six fabricated precedents; catching exactly that kind of error before it reaches a filing is now a real professional skill, not a footnote.
Precision drafting: contracts, pleadings, and legislative language

A single ambiguous clause in a contract or a poorly drafted pleading can cost a client real money or a case. This is the least glamorous, most consistently valuable skill across every branch of the field.
Client and stakeholder communication under pressure

Corporate, in-house, and judiciary work all reward people who can explain a risk, a delay, or a bad outcome clearly and calmly to a client, a business team, or a courtroom, not just people who know the law.
Regulatory and compliance literacy in one sector

Generalist legal knowledge is common; sector-specific regulatory depth, fintech, data protection, competition law, environmental compliance, is scarcer and pays a real premium in both firm and in-house roles.
AI verification judgment, not blind use of AI tools

The Bar Council of India has directed law schools to add AI to the curriculum, but using an AI research tool and knowing when to override or double-check it are different skills. The graduates who build the second one are the ones firms and in-house teams will trust with real client work sooner.

blocks.heading: Why This Question Needs a Field-Level Answer

items.text: A litigator, a corporate transactional associate, a compliance officer, a judge, and a law professor all hold the same base credential and do almost entirely different jobs.
Pay ranges across these branches do not overlap much at entry level: a first-year litigation junior and a first-year Tier-1 firm associate can be earning ten to fifteen times apart.

Regulation is reshaping the field mid-career for current students, the judiciary's 2025 practice-first rule and the Bar Council's still-developing AI-conduct rules both changed the ground rules in the last two years.

Unlike medicine or CA, there is no single unifying licensing exam GATE at the very start; AIBE and state bar enrolment matter for practice, but several branches, in-house, LPO, policy, academia, do not strictly require them at all.

blocks.heading: Actually Changing in Law Right Now

items.text: High-volume document review and first-pass due diligence in M&A, real estate, and litigation discovery, now standard AI-assisted work at most mid-to-large firms and LPOs.
Boilerplate contract drafting and clause-matching against a standard template.
Summarising case law and statutes for a first-draft research memo.

blocks.heading: What to Tell a Worried Family

items.text: Fear that "law" only means courtroom work, with the well-known uncertainty of early litigation income.
Stories about junior lawyers struggling financially in the first few years.
Not knowing whether an NLU seat, a private college, or a 3-year route after another degree matters most for a specific target branch.
